statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 8% (low). NQZ26 prints 31,074.50 on Yahoo Finance at 04:16Z and 31,069.50 on Investing.com, up only 0.04% and 0.02% against a 31,061.75 prior close, about 15 points above the 31,059.00 session low and 147 points below a 31,221.25 high that has now gone unretested for more than two hours. ES at -0.08% and YM at -0.13% sit at their own session lows, so no aligned one-way complex exists. Stress eases to 54% (elevated) as Brent 101.29 (-0.94%) and WTI 89.78 (-1.46%) press session lows despite a Strait of Hormuz effectively closed at Day 218. Confidence 88% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours, with a 7% floor and a 12% peak. The narrow danger window spans 13:00-15:00Z on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z and September ISM Services at 14:00Z. That window is published on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected.
headline: Tail eases to 8% as the NQ round-trip holds for a second hour and ES and YM tip to session lows, with Brent and WTI fading peak Gulf rhetoric at their own lows to pull Stress to 54%
body:
The round-trip identified in the previous assessment has now held for a second consecutive hour, and that persistence is the most important observation here. NQZ26 prints 31,074.50 on Yahoo Finance at 04:16:44Z and 31,069.50 on Investing.com, up 12.75 and 7.75 points against a 31,061.75 prior close, a gain of 0.04% and 0.02% on 44.83k contracts. The session range remains 31,059.00 to 31,221.25. Price has not merely retraced the overnight advance, it has spent a further hour basing roughly 15 points above the session low without reabsorbing any of it, and the 31,221.25 high has been left unchallenged for more than two hours.

The contract names shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements and holding near session extremes as the amplifiers that justify protection. None is present. The extension failed once, the retracement went the full distance back through the prior close, and no second attempt has been made. Mean reversion did not merely occur; it completed and then held. Tail therefore eases a further two points to 8%, mapping to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal.

The cross-asset picture has strengthened that read rather than complicating it. ES has tipped to 7,771.00, down 0.08% and sitting at a 7,769.50 session low, and YM is at 51,408.00, down 0.13% and also at its low. The entire index-futures complex is therefore flat to mildly negative and clustered at the bottom of a narrow overnight range. At the same time the Nikkei 225 is 2.31% higher at 69,886.50, having earlier crossed 70,000 for the first time in three months on a 5.7% gain in Tokyo Electron and 4.5% in Advantest. That melt-up has produced precisely no transmission into the Nasdaq-100, and the Topix gain of only 1.16% shows the Japanese move is narrow and semiconductor-concentrated rather than a broad regional risk impulse. A 2.3% regional advance that NQ declines to follow is strong evidence against a developing one-way global path.

The energy complex is cooling for a third consecutive hour, which is what pulls Stress down. Brent trades 101.29, down 0.94% in a 101.18 to 103.39 range, and WTI trades 89.78, down 1.46% in an 89.69 to 91.85 range. Both are at their session lows, and Brent has come off the 102.54 print recorded for 4 October. This is happening against the most aggressive available rhetoric: the Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed at Day 218 with a single transit recorded on 27 September against an 85-per-day baseline and 247 vessels holding position, further tankers have been struck, and an Iranian lawmaker has publicly targeted oil above 110 dollars. Crude is fading all of it, helped by a G7 release of up to 100 million barrels of emergency stocks and by OPEC+ holding November quotas unchanged. When the primary transmission channel for a geopolitical shock declines to transmit, the correct response is to lower Stress and leave Tail alone, not to raise Tail on the existence of the conflict. Stress eases to 54%, still elevated, because a 100-dollar Brent, a closed strait and a softening labour market remain a genuinely difficult environment.

The macro backdrop is supportive rather than threatening. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported September payrolls at plus 29,000 against an 84,000 consensus, with unemployment rising to 4.2%, downward revisions of 60,000 across the prior two months, and average hourly earnings up 0.1% to 37.81 dollars for 3.0% annual growth, the slowest since 2021. Yields retreated on that print; the H.15 series last published 4.78% at two years and 5.24% at ten years for 1 October, both lower than 30 September. The Nasdaq Composite closed 1.35% higher at a record on Friday with Nvidia at a record of its own, and the VIX finished at 15.31, down 6.59%. A falling-yield, low-volatility backdrop is the opposite of the aligned cross-asset configuration that would amplify Tail.

Confidence rises to 88%. Two independent live NQ quotes, live ES, YM, Brent and WTI prints, a live Nikkei quote, primary BLS employment data, the H.15 yield series and verified Gulf shipping status together form a dense and current evidence set, and the open question from the previous hour has now been resolved by observation rather than inference. The limits are honest ones: cash VIX and cash Treasuries are closed, H.15 lags by a session, and the shared Finviz context file was 7,511 minutes old with a partial collection status, so it was treated as unusable and this assessment rests entirely on independent research.

The published path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. It decays to a 7% floor as the Asian session is assumed to mature, allows 9% for the European cash-open liquidity transition, returns to the floor through the European morning, and rises to 11% and a 12% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours that carry the US cash open, the S&P Global finals and September ISM Services. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not claims about structure that cannot yet be observed. The path then decays through the US afternoon, allows 10% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to the floor across the assumed 21:00Z maintenance halt, and holds 8% through the overnight handoff into 6 October.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history. Tail was held at 3% from 04:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Tail then rose through the Sunday reopen as the overnight drift extended and a shallow pullback was absorbed: 12% in the 22:00Z slot, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October. It eased to 13% at 02:00Z once the fresh 31,221.25 high failed and to 10% at 03:00Z once the retracement completed. Stress ran a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings into the 14:00Z trough as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and then settled at 66%, 65%, 64%, 62%, 60% and 57% across the six reopen hours. Confidence held a narrow 83% to 88% band, densest in the European and early US hours and easing into the thin weekend and reopen hours.
outlookSummary: The completed round-trip has now held for a second hour. NQZ26 prints 31,074.50 and 31,069.50 across two independent feeds, up only 0.04% and 0.02%, basing about 15 points above the 31,059.00 session low with the 31,221.25 high unretested for over two hours, while ES at -0.08% and YM at -0.13% sit at their own session lows and a 2.31% Nikkei advance produces no transmission. A held retracement against an unfollowed regional melt-up is why Tail eases to 8% and Stress to 54%, with Brent 101.29 and WTI 89.78 at session lows despite Hormuz being effectively closed at Day 218. Tail carries 8% through the final Tokyo hour, where the 31,059.00 low is the invalidation level, then decays to a 7% floor as the Asian session is assumed to mature into two-way trade. It ticks to 9% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to the floor through the European morning, builds through the pre-market hours, and rises to 11% and a 12% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours carrying the US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals and September ISM Services. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances rather than observed structure. The path decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 10% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to the 7% floor across the assumed 21:00Z maintenance halt, and holds 8% across the overnight handoff into the Tokyo session on 6 October.

Stress edges to 55% because the European session is where a Gulf headline would most directly re-price the energy complex into equities.

The second European hour is the quietest expected liquidity window of the published path, so Tail sits at the 7% floor on the assumption that discovery stays orderly and retracements continue. The floor is deliberately not zero: a 218-day Hormuz closure retains a genuine gap-and-go discontinuity mechanism at any hour.
